title: The ALMA Survey of 70 μm Dark High-mass Clumps in Early Stages (ASHES). II. Molecular Outflows in the Extreme Early Stages of Protocluster Formation
question: Identify molecular outflows and study their properties, episodicity, accretion history, and feedback impact in extremely early evolutionary stages of high-mass star and protocluster formation.

data.sensitivity: ~0.1 mJy beam^-1 (continuum); ~0.06 K per 0.17 km s^-1 channel (first six lines); ~0.02 K per 1.3 km s^-1 channel (last four lines)

what.value: High-mass clumps outflow mechanical forces and L_bol/M_clump comparison sample

what.value: Identified dust continuum dense cores and their masses

evidence.quote: Clump fragmentation, based on the dust continuum emission, is presented in Sanhueza et al. (2019).
The error bars of _M_ core correspond to its uncertainty of 50% (Sanhueza et al. 2017, 2019).

recipe.goal: Identify molecular outflows and determine core systemic velocities
recipe.method: Visual inspection of 12m-only CO PPV data cubes in DS9 to determine blue/red-shifted velocity ranges, followed by moment-0 maps, channel maps, line profiles, and PV diagrams along outflow axes to refine velocity ranges and lobes. Core systemic velocities measured from centroid velocity of N2D+ 3-2 (or DCO+ 3-2, C18O 2-1).
key_parameters: Velocity range threshold > 2 sigma (rms in line-free channels); outflow lobe contour threshold > 4 sigma (rms of integrated intensity map)

recipe.goal: Compute outflow physical parameters and protostellar accretion rates
recipe.method: Calculate CO column density, outflow mass, momentum, energy, dynamical timescale, outflow rate, luminosity, and mechanical force from combined (12m+7m+TP) primary-beam-corrected CO 2-1 data using Equations A1-A8. Derive protostellar accretion rate from mechanical force assuming momentum conservation in a wind-driven outflow.
assumptions: LTE and optically thin CO line wing emission; excitation temperature approximated by dust temperature
CO-to-H2 abundance = 10^-4; mean molecular mass m_H2 = 2.72 m_H; uncorrected for inclination
Ratio of mass accretion rate to wind mass ejection rate k = 3; wind velocity v_w = 500 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Measure episodic ejection knot dynamical timescales
recipe.method: Visually follow contours in CO PV diagrams along outflow axes to define projected distance (lambda_knot) and velocity (v_knot) of emission knots, and compute dynamical timescales t_knot = lambda_knot / v_knot and inter-knot time spans Delta t_knot.
key_parameters: Uncertainties estimated as 2 km s^-1 for velocities (3x channel width) and 0''.5 for lengths (half angular resolution)

recipe.goal: Evaluate outflow-driven turbulence and cloud gravitational binding energy
recipe.method: Compute clump turbulent energy E_turb (Equations 1-2), turbulent dissipation time t_diss using two approaches (Equation 4 from McKee & Ostriker 2007 and Equation 5 from Mac Low 1999), turbulent dissipation rate E_dot_turb (Equation 3), ratio r_L = L_out / E_dot_turb, and gravitational binding energy E_grav = G M_cl^2 / R_cl.
assumptions: Average volume density rho = 3 M_cl / (4 pi R_cl^3); outflow lobe length approximates turbulence driving wavelength lambda_d

recipe.goal: Analyze SiO 5-4 column densities, abundances, and shock origins
recipe.method: Compute SiO column densities assuming optically thin LTE emission, derive SiO abundances using H2 column densities from CO, and inspect CO and SiO spectra and PV diagrams across SiO emission regions.
assumptions: Optically thin and LTE conditions for SiO 5-4 emission

score_reason: The ALMA project code, CASA versions, weighting, and analytic equations for outflow and turbulence parameters are clearly stated, and Paper I (Sanhueza et al. 2019) provides the core catalog and observational setup; however, visual outflow boundary definitions in DS9 and the omission of Tables 1-3 in the provided text prevent exact numerical reproduction without external tables and spatial masks.
